title: Auto-Renewal on a Renegotiated Vendor Contract
scenario_text:
You are a procurement manager at Volga Logistics reviewing the 'Alder Freight Systems' warehousing contract, which was executed in 2024 under the old contracting standard and contains a 3-year auto-renewal clause. The renewal window is approaching and the operations team wants clarity before it lapses, because Alder runs a regional distribution hub that Volga cannot easily re-source on short notice.

Active policy: Vendor Contracting Standard VCS-3, effective 2025-01-01, which replaced VCS-2. Under VCS-2, auto-renewal clauses of up to 3 years were permitted and renewed without additional sign-off. VCS-3 caps auto-renewal at 1 year and requires Procurement Director sign-off for any renewal. Transition clause: 'Contracts executed under VCS-2 retain their original auto-renewal terms for the duration of the current contract term. Any new contract, or any renegotiation of an existing contract, is governed by VCS-3.'

Variant facts: At this renewal point Volga is renegotiating the Alder contract — updating pricing and adding a new scope of warehousing services beyond the original agreement. The business wants to carry a multi-year auto-renewal forward onto the renegotiated agreement to lock in continuity. A coordinator asks whether a 3-year auto-renewal can proceed and whether Procurement Director sign-off is needed. There is no emergency or expedited-review flag on the file, and no other vendor is being evaluated.
question: Does the 3-year auto-renewal remain valid, and is Procurement Director sign-off required?
changed_fact: In the base, Volga is simply continuing the existing contract for its current term with no changes, which the transition clause grandfathers under VCS-2. In the variant, Volga is renegotiating the contract (new pricing and added scope), which the transition clause routes to VCS-3.
